To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the LOSP can decay to a goldstino and a higgs bosons if the goldstino is not constrained by supercurrent interactions, (2) this decay can occur even for LOSPs that are predominantly bino-like, and (3) the goldstino can be light and long-lived, and therefore can escape the detector

(a) in SUSY models with multiple sectors that break SUSY, LOSP decays are substantially modified by additional operators that are suppressed by the SUSY-breaking scale, (b) these additional operators can be enhanced by a U(1)_R symmetry, (c) the additional operators can mediate LOSP decays with a near 100\% branching fraction to the higgs and an uneaten Goldstino, (d) the higgs can be produced with a large boost
(i) the presence of uneaten goldstinos can dramatically modify the LOSP decay modes, and (ii) the presence of a gauged U(1) symmetry can enhance the goldstino-mediated decays of the LOSP.
